title: Greek yogurt chicken salad wrap
summary: Chicken salad with yogurt standing in for mayo. Same creaminess, roughly a third of the calories, and about 15 g more protein.

time.note: Assumes cooked chicken - leftovers, a rotisserie bird, or yesterday's tandoori.

ingredients.note: Small amount, big difference - it is what stops the yogurt tasting like plain yogurt.

steps: Mix the yogurt, mustard, lemon, salt and pepper into a dressing first, in the bottom of the bowl. Taste it now - once the chicken is in it is harder to correct.
Fold in the chicken, spring onion, cucumber and anything else. Do not overmix or it turns pasty.
Warm the wraps for 20 seconds in a dry pan - they crack if you roll them cold.
Lay lettuce down first (it keeps the wrap from going soggy), then the chicken salad in a line just below the centre.
Fold the sides in, then roll tight from the bottom. Cut on the diagonal.
tips: The filling keeps three days in the fridge. Assemble the wrap only when you are eating it.
Works just as well on toast, in a lettuce cup, or over a salad with no wrap at all.
Poach chicken specifically for this: cover with cold salted water, bring to a bare simmer, 12 minutes, then let it cool in the liquid. Stays far juicier than boiling.
health_notes: Two tablespoons of mayo is about 190 calories and no protein. The same amount of Greek yogurt is roughly 20 calories and 3 g of protein. This one swap is most of the difference here.

source.adapted: Deli chicken salad with the mayo base replaced entirely by Greek yogurt.
